scope: Four asserted propositions; frozen 73-case snapshot; PSY/SKL excluded; no live programme inspection or mutation

propositions.asserted_proposition: Material and production performance are task-dependent; older practices can coexist with new inputs rather than follow a universal replacement sequence.
propositions.status: useful conditional proposition; no confirmed overreach in its stated scope
propositions.falsification_attempt: Ask whether coexistence is explained equally well by restricted purchasing power, cheap unpaid labour or state allocation rather than superior task fit.

evidence.observation: Material tests support trade-offs, while the paper explicitly requires better reproducibility for elongation data.
Reusable blocks and separable work stages are documented; cross-country costs also vary with paper, wages, premises and patronage.

Pre-1949 mixed yarn supports coexistence. Later Zhouzhi households sold cloth coupons and continued homespun amid cash scarcity and state procurement. The later period is a separate negative case, not evidence about the earlier episode.

propositions.independent_premises: Alloy composition and treatment; material failure; documented workflows; dated input use. Historical chooser weights and opportunity costs are not measured.
propositions.sequence_and_reverse_causality: Physical tests establish a properties mechanism, not why historical users selected an alloy. Hybrid use cannot determine whether preferences, poverty or institutions produced persistence.
propositions.rival_discrimination: A single physical ranking fails; comparative importance of task properties versus constraints remains underdetermined.
propositions.explanatory_value: A valid empirical rejection of automatic replacement and an engineering mechanism. It is not an empirical causal law of historical adoption.
propositions.acceptance_check: Keep the existing explicit non-optimality/non-consent caveat. Do not read evaluated as identification of the historical uptake mechanism; no causal estimate is required for the modest existence claim.

propositions.asserted_proposition: Risk and costs outside acquisition price can change investment comparisons; the Ghana trial supports a risk constraint under the tested contracts.
propositions.status: useful locally discriminating causal evidence; general constraint ranking unknown
propositions.falsification_attempt: Test whether cash changes some inputs despite the aggregate result, whether insurance is simply another transfer, and whether demand for the complement itself persists.

evidence.observation: Randomized treatment precedes investment. Table IV total-cost estimates are 266.15 for insured and 2.44 for cash alone; chemical-input estimates are 37.90 and 55.63 respectively, both statistically significant. Treatment intensity is not directly comparable.

propositions.independent_premises: Assigned cash/insurance and randomized prices are observed independently of investment, not inferred from uptake.
propositions.sequence_and_reverse_causality: Assignment avoids investment causing its own treatment. State-contingent income, expectations and selection in purchase still limit mechanism decomposition.
propositions.rival_discrimination: Insurance-only investment weakens a cash-shortfall-only explanation. The input composition contrast blocks an across-input ranking; it is not a statistically demonstrated reversal of the two coefficients.
propositions.explanatory_value: Explains a bounded difference with an observable intervention and rival prediction. Whole-use burden remains an accounting framework, not an estimated cross-domain law.
propositions.acceptance_check: Retain the Ghana sample/contract boundary and aggregate outcome. Do not paraphrase as cash never changes technology choices. Existing AGR-K15/16 caveats substantially meet this check.

propositions.asserted_proposition: Actor interests differ; the Chinese prescribing audit challenges a demand-only explanation by changing expected purchase location.
propositions.status: useful local mechanism support; independent source recheck partial
propositions.falsification_attempt: Ask whether outside purchase signals distrust, counterfeit risk or offense, and whether patient demand has an effect with hospital dispensing.

evidence.passage: Indexed full-text sections I and III; publisher extract of experiment 2
evidence.observation: Relative-pharmacy, knowledge and gift scripts probe nonfinancial signals. These strengthen the incentive account without eliminating every signal or measuring reform outcomes.

propositions.independent_premises: Assigned standardized scripts and encounter prescriptions precede inference about motives. Revenue expectation is manipulated indirectly.
propositions.sequence_and_reverse_causality: Randomized script order/roles reduce ordinary selection. Prescription outcomes cannot cause prior assignment. Script effect is firmer than isolated revenue-mechanism effect.
propositions.rival_discrimination: Demand-only is weakened; demand is not absent. Frozen MED-K22 itself reports a large request-associated increase when dispensing stays in hospital.
propositions.explanatory_value: More than an actor taxonomy: the within-study contrast predicts a different prescribing outcome. It remains a use-quality study, not evidence for historical diffusion rates.
propositions.acceptance_check: Keep causal-identification at encounter-script scope and mechanism-supported for revenue interpretation. Do not equate prescription with ingestion or resistance. Exact four percentages were read in frozen records but not independently reverified from a complete source table in this audit.

propositions.asserted_proposition: Recurring operation matters in these cases, without identifying maintenance as a universal or unique cause of persistence or reversal.
propositions.status: useful conditional proposition; historical cause shares honestly unknown
propositions.falsification_attempt: Look for service failure despite continuing inputs, clinical nulls despite high use, and reverse causality from weak demand to low repair.

evidence.observation: Repair effort and subsequent condition/use do not independently randomize maintenance; low valuation, design and use can jointly produce deterioration.
HAPIN achieved high supported use and lower exposure, but the birth-weight interval includes zero. This blocks explaining every clinical null by low use.

evidence.passage: Background; Reported causes; Sri Lanka paragraph
evidence.observation: The review allows structural changes that remove the need for active suppression. Sri Lanka sequence includes surveillance and movement; only 45/273 attributed causes had substantial analysis.

evidence.passage: Frozen ANC-K06 and source pp. 604-607 locator
evidence.observation: Continuing water with cessation rules out a simple complete-cutoff story; adequate discharge, demand and unique abandonment cause remain unresolved.

propositions.independent_premises: Equipment condition, programme chronology, exposure and clinical outcomes can be observed separately. No single maintenance quantity is shared across these systems.
propositions.sequence_and_reverse_causality: Demand can fall before upkeep; ecology can change with programme activity. Observed source sequence is not allocation of causal shares.
propositions.rival_discrimination: Rejects durable installation as sufficient for permanent service. Does not select neglect over changed demand/ecology, or turn service continuity into clinical success.
propositions.explanatory_value: A scoped recurring-input hypothesis and strong separation of endpoints; weakest of these four as an identified cross-case causal mechanism. The ledger already marks its test underdetermined.
propositions.acceptance_check: Retain SYNTHESIS line 63 and the underdetermined test status. Use HAPIN as the explicit countercase whenever the short narrative might suggest maintenance explains all null benefits.
